data.long_meaning: In Christian and Jewish traditions, the Messiah is the expected savior or redeemer of humanity. The term derives from the Hebrew māšîāḥ, meaning ‘anointed one’. The Greek term christos, meaning ‘anointed one’, gave rise to the English term ‘Christ’, which is commonly used to refer to Jesus. The name Messia carries the meaning “God's Anointed One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Messia usually hope their child will grow to embody god's anointed one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Messia total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
